base.collect: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED (21 Nov ~00:50 WIB): the escrow demand was FLAT abi.encode(address, bytes) (128 bytes). The arbiter's abi.decode(demand, (DemandData)) expects the NESTED form abi.encode(DemandData) (160 bytes, leading 0x20 tuple offset) — with the flat form it reads the oracle address as a tuple offset and reverts (oracle=0 accidentally decodes, which is why zero-input probes passed). Proof: decodeDemandData(nested) returns the exact (oracle, context); check(attestation, nested demand) == true for this very escrow. The escrow's demand is immutable in its attestation, so this escrow itself can never collect; its 0.002 ETH is reclaimable by the buyer after expiry 1795784903 (~27 Nov 2026). The corrected encoding is proven end-to-end by the ce-release-v4 escrow (collect tx 0x245dedc6...). Hypothesis by ChatGPT round 5; the 'partner defect' and 'version skew' framings are both RETRACTED — it was our encoding.

render_probe.conclusion: ROOT CAUSE OF SCENARIO B FOUND: web.render normalizes the fetched text (703 vs 706 chars), so the seller-pinned raw-file sha256 can never match inside DealJudge v3's resolve — the leader aborts deterministically on every node and every mode. The probe tx itself passed full consensus with strict cross-validator recomputation, proving fetches are consistent across validators; only the representation differs. Fix: DealJudge v4 fetches via web.get (raw body).
